 Hwang Jae-min Maintains Lead on Day Two of KPGA Tour Championship, Pursuing First Win at Age 40
 Son Geun-yeong 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.07 19:44 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ Hwang Jae-min, sole leader after the third round 
 Hwang Jae-min has maintained his lead for the second consecutive day at the Tour Championship, the final event of the KPGA Tour season, moving closer to his first regular tour victory. 
 During the third round of the tournament held at Teddy Valley Golf & Resort in Seogwipo, Jeju Island, Hwang managed his game without major mistakes despite strong winds of 10 meters per second. He shot an even par to finish at 6-under-par overall, standing alone at the top of the leaderboard with a one-stroke lead. 
 Hwang, who turns 40 years old on November 12, is eyeing his maiden victory in his 212th appearance on the regular tour. 
 Jeong Jae-hyun, who finished as runner-up after a playoff at the Lexus Masters last week, chased Hwang in a tie for second place alongside Jeon Sung-hyun at 5-under-par overall. 
 Kim Min-gyu, a three-time winner on the KPGA Tour, and Jeong Han-mil, who claimed his first win at the Gunsan CC Open last June, joined the title race by tying for third place, two strokes behind Hwang. 
 Shin Sang-hun, who ranks first in the Player of the Year (Daesang) points, fell to a tie for 40th, while Jeong Chan-min, ranked third, placed tied for 28th, slipping out of contention for the tournament title. However, the two players will continue their fierce battle for the grand prize in tomorrow's final round.
